title: Wall-mounted fixture and electrical boundaries (referral)
audience: Flat-pack and fixture installers who may be asked to mount items that need an electrical connection
learningOutcomes: Identify the wall-mounted fixtures whose electrical connection is referred to a licensed electrical worker.
Describe the safe response when an electrical connection is needed or a cable is found.
Record the referral without making any electrical connection.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NSW Government, Electricians: electrical licence for wiring work (last updated 1 December 2025); WorkSafe Queensland, Classes of electrical licences (no date shown); Energy Safe Victoria, Electrician's licence (A grade) (page dated 1 November 2026; reviewed 30 June 2025). The Victorian licence position has only been partly confirmed.

instruction.heading: Mounting is not the same as connecting
instruction.body: A wall-mounted item such as a television bracket, a wall light, a heated towel rail or a mirror with lighting may need an electrical connection. Mounting the item to the wall may be within your scope if the mounting is only structural and the item has no fixed electrical supply. Connecting it to a fixed circuit, running a new cable, or altering a switch is electrical work and is referred to a licensed electrical worker. Check the item's requirements before mounting, and stop if it needs a fixed supply that is not present.

instruction.heading: Stop and refer when a cable is found
instruction.body: If a cable is found while locating a fixing point, stop drilling in that area and do not move, cut or join it. Record the location and refer the connection to a licensed electrical worker. If the item needs a fixed electrical supply that is not at the wall, refer the supply to the licensed electrical worker and do not run a cable yourself. Complete the structural mounting only where the wall has been confirmed clear and the approver agrees.

procedure: Check the item's electrical requirement before mounting.
Mount the item only where the mounting is structural and the item needs no fixed supply.
If a fixed supply is needed, stop and refer the connection to a licensed electrical worker.
If a cable is found, stop drilling in that area, do not move it, and record the location.
Tell the client in writing which part of the installation was completed and which was referred.
Record the referral and the outcome.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks you to mount a wall light and wire it into the nearest switch.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Wiring a light into a switch is electrical wiring work, which in New South Wales needs an electrical licence regardless of the cost or type of work (NSW Government, last updated 1 December 2025). Refer the wiring to a licensed electrical worker. You may only mount the bracket if the mounting is structural and the approver agrees, and the completion record must show the electrical referral.

commonErrors.error: Wiring a fixture into a switch or circuit as part of mounting it.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer all connection to a fixed supply to a licensed electrical worker.

commonErrors.error: Cutting or moving a cable found behind the wall.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, leave it in place, record it, and refer.

commonErrors.error: Stating the whole installation is electrically complete after mounting.
commonErrors.prevention: Report the mounting as completed and the connection as referred.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: New South Wales: electrical wiring work needs an electrical licence regardless of the cost or type of work, except for equipment operating at not more than 50 volts AC or 120 volts ripple-free DC (NSW Government electrical licence page, last updated 23 June 2026).

Queensland: the open electrical work licence (electrical mechanic) covers installing wiring, and businesses doing electrical work for others need an electrical contractor licence. WorkSafe Queensland's classes page (no date shown) also says only an electrical contractor may do electrical work in a home. Victoria: Energy Safe Victoria issues electrician licences, and contracting for profit needs Registered Electrical Contractor registration (page dated 01/11/2026).
Completing this lesson does not give an electrical licence, certificate or authority to make an electrical connection.

qualityStandard: The item's electrical requirement is checked before mounting.
No connection to a fixed supply is made by an unlicensed worker.
Completed mounting and referred connection are reported separately.
documentationEvidence: Pre-mount check record showing the electrical requirement
Referral note for any connection or cable found
Written note to the client showing completed and referred work
summary: Mounting a bracket is not the same as connecting it to a supply.
Stop and refer any connection or cable found in the wall.
Report completed mounting and referred connection separately.
referencesAtEnd: Official sources to recheck before any job: NSW Government, Electricians: electrical licence for wiring work (last updated 1 December 2025); WorkSafe Queensland, Classes of electrical licences (no date shown); Energy Safe Victoria, Electrician's licence (A grade) (page dated 1 November 2026; reviewed 30 June 2025). The Victorian licence position has only been partly confirmed.

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks you to mount a wall light and wire it to a switch. What is correct?
options: Wire it because the mounting is done and the client expects the light to work today
Wire it using a different colour cable, since the cable colour does not change the safety of the job
Run a new cable from the switch yourself, since the route is short and the work is simple to do
Mount the bracket only where it is structural, and refer the wiring to a licensed electrical worker

knowledgeChecks.question: A cable is found while drilling for a bracket. What should happen?
options: Stop drilling in that area, do not move it, record it, and refer
Move it aside and continue drilling the next hole in the wall
Cut it and reconnect it with a joiner, then continue the work
Tape it and carry on with the bracket, since the tape is strong

knowledgeChecks.question: Who does the lesson say connects a wall light to a fixed circuit?
options: The installer, if the bracket is level
The client, using the supplied cable

officialReferences.covers: Electrical licence needed for wiring work regardless of cost or type; confirm the issuer and class on the NSW licence pages. Publisher: NSW Government.

officialReferences.title: Classes of electrical licences
officialReferences.covers: Open electrical work licence covers wiring; electrical contractor licence for work for others; the page does not name the issuer. Publisher: WorkSafe Queensland.

officialReferences.title: Electrician's licence (A grade)
officialReferences.covers: ESV issues the licence and contracting for profit needs REC registration; the page does not state the fixed-wiring scope. Publisher: Energy Safe Victoria.
